items.requirement: The new `pow` operation computes `a ** b` deterministically using standard IEEE-754 double-precision semantics, with no additional precondition/domain-error check introduced. Unlike `div`/`mod`, `pow` has no zero-divisor-style precondition, so OCL/tests must not invent one (e.g. must not reject `b <= 0` or `a == 0`).
items.rationale: Prior change `initial-calculator` established named `PreconditionError` for div/mod-by-zero; `pow` must not silently inherit that pattern where it does not apply, or later NFR/OCL work will over-generalize preconditions onto an operation that has none.
items.threshold: For all finite numeric `a`, `b` accepted by the existing `{op,a,b}` request shape, `pow` returns `a ** b` (JS `Math.pow`/`**` semantics) and never throws `PreconditionError`; malformed body still yields the existing generic 400, unchanged.

items.rationale: Sample / evaluation workload; `pow` is a single native exponentiation operation with negligible cost relative to existing ops.

items.rationale: solid_sdd evaluation path requires every in-scope operation to be machine-checkable, matching the precedent set for add/sub/mul/div/mod in `initial-calculator`.
